title: A convoy east of Formosa, 20–21 September 1944
eyebrow: South of Honshu and east of Formosa · BANG's third war patrol

participants.name: Convoy TAKA-909
participants.note: no record names the convoy BANG fired at; TAKA-909 sailed again from Keelung that morning and was at sea east of Keelung that night (its escort W-15's diary), the only convoy on those lanes that week

paras.text: BANG's last two attacks of her third patrol, on a convoy she found by its escorts' sound pinging, as typed on her attack sheets. The convoy was most likely TAKA-909, sailing again after BANG's attack of the 19th; its escort W-15's diary has it at sea that night and enters no attack.

BANG claimed an AO and an AK sunk and one damaged, as FRUPAC relayed it. No Japanese record has a loss that night. TAKA-909's escort W-15 sailed again from Keelung with the convoy at 06?0 I on the 20th (noon 25-01N 122-21E) and anchored at Miyako at 1530 I on the 21st (noon 24-51.5N 124-45E), entering nothing for the night between: no attack, no ship lost (p. 49–50) [[cite:jacar:C08030607800]]. By straight interpolation between those noon positions the convoy was some 25–30 nm west-south-west of BANG when she fired (ours, inferred); BANG's own track that day is dead reckoning too.
BANG made contact by the escorts' JK sound pinging at 35,000 yards.

Positions are BANG's own dead reckoning and star sights; lines between them are straight, and where she went in between is not recorded. Open circles are ships she sighted, at the target's position. As the clock passes each firing time a red ring pulses at BANG's position; hover a diamond for the attack sheet.
BANG kept zone K (−10) throughout. Japanese records use Tokyo time (I, −9).

Two Japanese records for this patrol give no time: combinedfleet.com's account of convoy No. 3905 and the 4th Surface Escort Division's daily summary for TAKA-909 (W-15's diary gives TAKA-909's, 0820 I). Each is drawn at the time of the attack it matches, and marked so. FRUPAC's intercept has No. 3905's ships "torp & sunk 1520/09" (1520 I = 1620 K, between Attacks 1 and 2).

No Japanese record names the convoy of Attacks 5 and 6 (20–21 September) or records them: the 4th Escort diary has no attack on those days, and W-15's diary, for the convoy most likely attacked, none that night. CD-30's diary (the convoy's other warship) has not been found on JACAR. Where the Japanese record names only the ships that were hit, the rest of the convoy is described as BANG saw it.

BANG's third war patrol report, NARA microfilm M1752 (74802831). The 4th Surface Escort Division / Okinawa Base Force war diary, September 1944, and minesweeper W-15's war diary, September 1944, via JACAR (C08030144100, C08030607800, National Institute for Defense Studies). Convoy No. 3905 from combinedfleet.com, a secondary source, flagged where used. Coastline: Natural Earth.

events.note: The Navy's day-by-day summary of escort and anti-submarine events, September 1944, narrative for the 20th (same page as J04). The character before ×4 (probably the aircraft type) is not read. No position, no convoy name and no ship hit. The day's other entry, 1840 I, is Hatsuharu's attack on a submarine about 30 nm WSW of Iki (壱岐), off Kyushu, not in this area. Zone not stated; taken as I (Tokyo), assumed

outcome.note: TAKA-909 put back to Keelung after the 19th's attack and sailed again on the morning of the 20th for Naha by way of Miyako (W-15's diary, J08, J09): the convoy BANG found that afternoon (1555 I at 25-07N 122-57E) and attacked that night is most likely this one (inferred: the only convoy on the Keelung lanes that week, J06, and W-15's noon positions put it some 25-30 nm from her by straight interpolation). W-15's diary enters no attack and no loss that night, and the convoy reached Miyako the next afternoon. BANG claimed an AK and an AO sunk

paras.text: Attacked by BANG on 19 September 1944 off the north-east coast of Formosa. The Okinawa diary names six escorts and the one ship lost, No. 2 Tosei Maru, and says CD-30 and Taian Maru with army aircraft attacked the submarine and claimed it sunk. BANG surfaced that night after about 80 depth charges.

**Route and size** from the 4th Surface Escort Division's table of convoys given air cover (jacar:C08030144100 p05, read on the image 5 Nov 2026): on the 19th, TAKA-909, ten ships of 34,049 tons, escorted by CD-30, W-15, No. 3 Takunan Maru, Shichiri Maru, Taian Maru and No. 3 Taihei Maru, routed Keelung to Kagoshima and Naha to Kagoshima. So it sailed from Keelung, not Takao as the convoy code had suggested. Its sailing time and cargo are not recorded. The waypoints off Formosa's east coast and Kagoshima Bay are assumed. BANG counted eight merchantmen, one an oiler.

No other US boat's attack on TAKA-909 has been found: the diary's columns for the 18th–21st have only this attack and, on the 20th, an attack on the depot ship Jingei far to the east (N27-12.5 E127-10.0; not BANG's).

**The escort W-15's diary** (jacar:C08030607800, September 1944, read on the images 11 Nov 2026) gives the voyage: sailed from Keelung for Naha at 0210 on the 19th; No. 7 ship Tosei Maru torpedoed at 0820 at 24-52N 122-23E (p53); W-15 led the convoy back to Keelung, anchoring at 2000. The convoy sailed again at 06?0 on the 20th (noon 25-01N 122-21E), anchored at Miyako at 1530 on the 21st (noon 24-51.5N 124-45E), sailed again that evening, and dispersed off Naha at 1350 on the 23rd, W-15 entering at 1520 (p49-p50). No attack is entered for the night of the 20th, when BANG fired at a convoy east of Keelung (engagement `bang-east-of-formosa-1944-09-20`). Times I.
To find: TAKA-909's ships' names and cargo (CD-30's or the other escorts' September diaries, not found on JACAR).

words.type_attack: Night surface. Fired six bow tubes, spread 1° between torpedoes by means of the offset knob on the TDC at three over-lapping targets, ranges 2200 to 3900 yards.
words.description: Convoy consisting of one AO (very long (450 ft. by binocular formula) and low, with stack extremely aft, best estimate, RIKKO MARU, ONI 208J (revised) page 283); five unidentified medium merchantmen; and three or more escorts, probably CHIDORI type. Fired at three over-lapping merchantmen. Moonless night with about 30% overcast.
words.determined_by: Heard three hits from salvo of six torpedoes. Saw flash in two different targets from two of the hits. Tracked one pip detached from rest of convoy and stopped, and pip disappearing. Radar reported another pip disappearing but evidence of sinking not considered positive.
words.target_line: Target Draft: 24 feet Course: 100° Speed: 8.0 Range: *2200 yds (to 1st) *3000 yds (to 2nd) *3900 yds (to 3rd) *Targets over-lapping.
words.remarks: This attack, firing the entire nest of bow tubes into a group of over-lapping targets, is not considered to be as good as making a series of individual attacks at definitely selected targets, but the proximity and maneuvers of the escort led me to believe that I had been detected (possibly by radar interference, in which my exact position was not known) and that I would soon have the escort on me; and I wanted to inflict as much damage as possible before this occurred.
words.note: Three ranges are typed, one to each overlapping target; attacks.csv gives the first (2200), the sheet not saying which torpedoes went to which target. The gyro angles of tubes 3, 2 and 1 are typed with an asterisk (*355, *350, *345), keyed to the sheet's note "Swung right after 3rd torpedo fired"; attacks.csv holds the numbers. The sheet types only the one own course, 335, so those three tracks (56S, 58S, 60S) do not follow from 335 + gyro against 100 (50S, 45S, 40S): they fit an own course of about 341, 346 and 351 as the boat swung. Kept as typed. Tubes were fired from the bottom up, 6 first (remarks of Attack 6).

words.type_attack: Same approach as for attack No. 5. Immediately after firing bow tubes swung right and opened outer doors on stern tubes, at this time did not know whether I would be escaping from the escort or firing at the tanker which was the trailing ship in the south column. Immediately after first bow torpedo hit, tanker swung right. I steadied with him sharp on my port quarter and as his angle on the bow passed through 90° fired four stern tubes spread 1½, ½, ½, 1½ from aft forward by means of the offset knob on the TDC.
words.description: Same convoy as Attack No. 5. Fired at the AO.
words.sunk: One AO (similar to RIKKO MARU). EU.
words.determined_by: Heard two hits in this target. Saw target sinking and enveloped in dense smoke. Pip of this target soon disappeared from radar screen.
words.target_line: Target Draft: 29 feet Course: 230° Speed: 8.0 Range: 1700 yds.
words.remarks: Misses due to target continuing to swing during torpedo run. On attacks 5 and 6 fired lower tubes first because I believe they afford less chance of detection on launching.
words.note: The sheet's time is typed "0017-15(K)" (15 seconds after 0017); positions.csv has 0017. attacks.csv keeps 0017-15. The type-attack paragraph gives the spread as 1½, ½, ½, 1½ (1° between torpedoes), as does the table's "Divergent, 1° between torpedoes".
